source_text: Mihi interim abunde sufficit, etiam per hoc ipsum probare, nusquam te in sacris Litteris legisse quod credis, quod tu in tali causa nihil praeter episcopi, quas dicis, dictiunculas protulisti; quibus si aliquid auctoratius potuisses offendere, ab his procul dubio temperasses.
pass_a_gloss: For me meanwhile it abundantly suffices even through this itself to prove that you have nowhere in the sacred Letters read what you believe, because you in such a cause brought forth nothing besides the little sayings of a bishop, as you call them; from which if you had been able to meet something more authoritative, you would without doubt have abstained.

lemmas.lexica: LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: For the present, it is more than enough for me to prove even from this that you have nowhere read your belief in the sacred writings: in so important a case, you have produced nothing except the bishop’s little sayings, as you call them. If you had been able to find anything more authoritative, you would undoubtedly have left these alone.

choices.why: Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
